From 74b4dbb946060a3233604d91859a9abd3708141d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Andreas Gruenbacher <agruenba@redhat.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 12:14:30 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] gfs2: prevent NULL pointer dereference during unmount

When flushing out outstanding glock work during an unmount, gfs2_log_flush()
can be called when sdp->sd_jdesc has already been deallocated and sdp->sd_jdesc
is NULL.  Commit 35264909e9d1 ("gfs2: Fix NULL pointer dereference in
gfs2_log_flush") added a check for that to gfs2_log_flush() itself, but it
missed the sdp->sd_jdesc dereference in gfs2_log_release().  Fix that.

Reported-by: kernel test robot <lkp@intel.com>
Reported-by: Dan Carpenter <error27@gmail.com>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/r/202604071139.HNJiCaAi-lkp@intel.com/
Fixes: 35264909e9d1 ("gfs2: Fix NULL pointer dereference in gfs2_log_flush")
Signed-off-by: Andreas Gruenbacher <agruenba@redhat.com>

diff --git a/fs/gfs2/log.c b/fs/gfs2/log.c
index 3a01d4e7667a..78bba8cc10b8 100644
--- a/fs/gfs2/log.c
+++ b/fs/gfs2/log.c
@@ -467,8 +467,9 @@ void gfs2_log_release(struct gfs2_sbd *sdp, unsigned int blks)
 {
 	atomic_add(blks, &sdp->sd_log_blks_free);
 	trace_gfs2_log_blocks(sdp, blks);
-	gfs2_assert_withdraw(sdp, atomic_read(&sdp->sd_log_blks_free) <=
-				  sdp->sd_jdesc->jd_blocks);
+	gfs2_assert_withdraw(sdp, !sdp->sd_jdesc ||
+			atomic_read(&sdp->sd_log_blks_free) <=
+			sdp->sd_jdesc->jd_blocks);
 	if (atomic_read(&sdp->sd_log_blks_needed))
 		wake_up(&sdp->sd_log_waitq);
 }
-- 
2.34.1

The patch introduces a single change in the file `fs/gfs2/log.c` to prevent a NULL pointer dereference during unmount.

**Modifications in each file:**

- **fs/gfs2/log.c** (in function `gfs2_log_release`):  
  The condition inside `gfs2_assert_withdraw` is updated from:  
  `atomic_read(&sdp->sd_log_blks_free) <= sdp->sd_jdesc->jd_blocks`  
  to:  
  `!sdp->sd_jdesc || atomic_read(&sdp->sd_log_blks_free) <= sdp->sd_jdesc->jd_blocks`  
  This ensures that if `sdp->sd_jdesc` is `NULL` (which can happen during unmount after journal descriptor deallocation), the assertion is skipped rather than causing a crash by dereferencing the NULL pointer.

**Relationships between the modifications:**

The fix addresses a gap left by a previous commit (`35264909e9d1`), which added a NULL pointer check in `gfs2_log_flush()` but missed a similar dereference in `gfs2_log_release()`. Both functions are called during unmount when flushing glock work, and both can encounter a deallocated `sd_jdesc`. This patch complements the earlier fix by applying the same defensive check in the overlooked location, thereby fully preventing the NULL pointer dereference scenario during unmount.

gfs2: prevent NULL pointer dereference during unmount

When flushing out outstanding glock work during an unmount, gfs2_log_flush()
can be called when sdp->sd_jdesc has already been deallocated and sdp->sd_jdesc
is NULL.  Commit 35264909e9d1 ("gfs2: Fix NULL pointer dereference in

missed the sdp->sd_jdesc dereference in gfs2_log_release().  Fix that.

Reported-by: kernel test robot <lkp@intel.com>
Reported-by: Dan Carpenter <error27@gmail.com>

Signed-off-by: Andreas Gruenbacher <agruenba@redhat.com>

Here is the root cause:
During unmount, gfs2_log_flush() may be called after the journal descriptor (sd_jdesc) has been freed and set to NULL. A previous fix added a NULL check in gfs2_log_flush() but not in gfs2_log_release(), causing a NULL pointer dereference when gfs2_log_release() attempts to access sd_jdesc->jd_blocks.

Here is the patch:
 
 void gfs2_log_release(struct gfs2_sbd *sdp, unsigned int blks)
 {
 	atomic_add(blks, &sdp->sd_log_blks_free);
 	trace_gfs2_log_blocks(sdp, blks);
-	gfs2_assert_withdraw(sdp, atomic_read(&sdp->sd_log_blks_free) <=
-				  sdp->sd_jdesc->jd_blocks);
+	gfs2_assert_withdraw(sdp, !sdp->sd_jdesc ||
+			atomic_read(&sdp->sd_log_blks_free) <=
+			sdp->sd_jdesc->jd_blocks);
 	if (atomic_read(&sdp->sd_log_blks_needed))
 		wake_up(&sdp->sd_log_waitq);
 }

				  sdp->sd_jdesc->jd_blocks);
</text>
Reason:
During unmount, `sdp->sd_jdesc` can be NULL after it has been freed and set to NULL. This statement dereferences `sdp->sd_jdesc->jd_blocks` without a NULL check, causing a NULL pointer dereference.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>
gfs2_assert_withdraw(sdp, !sdp->sd_jdesc ||
			atomic_read(&sdp->sd_log_blks_free) <=
			sdp->sd_jdesc->jd_blocks);
</text>
Reason:
The fix adds a short-circuit condition `!sdp->sd_jdesc` before accessing `sd_jdesc->jd_blocks`. When `sd_jdesc` is NULL, the condition evaluates to true, avoiding the dereference. If `sd_jdesc` is not NULL, the original comparison is safely performed. This prevents the NULL pointer dereference while preserving the assertion logic.
